validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented, non-GEM. Found a primary EIB-published Environmental Impact Assessment (PETROSAFE, November 2007) titled 'GASCO Abr Sinai Onshore Gas Pipeline' (https://www.eib.org/files/pipeline/20070088_eia4_en.pdf) describing a 2007-2009 duplication project. Its Section 3.1 states verbatim (confirmed via pdftotext -layout after url_verifier's automated substring check FAILed on this large PDF -- a documented false-negative class per url_verifier.py's own docstring, not evidence of absence): pipeline starts 'from the existed valve room of El-Tena East site... heads south... crossing El-Qantar - Port Foad Road, and continue parallel to El-Sheikh Gaber Canal... to reach El-Qantar-El-Areish road... in the back area of Roman village to be connected to Roman compressing station... (End point of Loop 1, from KM 0.00 to KM 33.00)'. This is an exact name/endpoint match for this row's segment ('El Tena East-Roman Pipeline'). The purpose statement names the pipe 'Abr Sinai 36", 111 KM' -- Arabic 'Abr Sinai' = 'Trans/Across Sinai', matching the row's English name 'Abr Sina(i)'. CLASSIFICATION: transmission is correct -- a 36in trunk line feeding a named compressing station as part of GASCO's national gas grid, not a gathering/distribution line; both the EIA and the sheet's own EGAS Annual Report 2018 map agree it is a gas (not NGL/oil) line. STATUS: confirmed operating via TWO tests, neither of them a text match on the word 'operating' (which never appears, correctly noted by the automated check on the map PDF): (1) the EIA's own Table 3.2 project schedule runs 01-Nov-2007 to 31-Jul-2009, 17 years before today's audit; (2) VISUAL/COLOR test on the sheet's own cited source -- fetched the cached page-35 crop of this exact EGAS Annual Report 2018 PDF (already on file in this batch's archive from a prior route-creation pass) and confirmed the El-Tina-to-Sinai corridor is drawn in the map's own 'Existing P/L' green, not the 'Under Cons.' red or 'Under study' blue used elsewhere on the same map -- i.e. the map's own legend, read visually rather than as searchable text, supports 'operating'. DIAMETER: 36in matches exactly in both the EIA and the map. DUPLICATE CHECK (per the DUPLICATE/IDENTITY WATCHLIST): NOT the same pipe as P8013 'Trans Sinai Gas Pipeline I' despite the name-family collision -- independently confirmed the sibling shard's finding that P8013 is actually a 12in Gulf-of-Suez CROSSING line (Petreco Plant->Ras Bakr Transmission Station, named 'Trans Gulf Gas' in its own best source, not 'Abr Sinai'/'Trans Sinai'): different corridor, different diameter (12in vs 36in), different literal name. NOT the same pipe as P8044 'Abr Sinai Gas Pipeline I' either, even though both are part of the SAME 2007-2009 GASCO duplication project and same family name -- P8044 is the EIA's separate 'Loop 2' (Bair El-Abd->El-Areish, ~78km), a distinct, non-adjoining segment starting ~37 km further east of this row's Roman endpoint (geodesic Roman-to-Bair El-Abd = 36.9 km, computed from the EIA's own coordinates), i.e. the sheet's split into two rows for the two loops is the correct granularity, not a double-count of one physical pipe.

validity.researcher_notes: MATERIAL LENGTH DISAGREEMENT, not a rounding difference. The sheet gives LengthKnown=55.00 km for 'El Tena East-Roman Pipeline'. The EIB EIA for this exact segment (same document as above) is explicit and precise: 'Loop 1, from KM 0.00 to KM 33.00' -- 33 km, sourced from a construction-phase chainage tied to two named, coordinated endpoints (El-Tena East valve room and Roman compressing station), not a schematic estimate. Three independent checks all point the same direction: (1) GEODESIC -- haversine distance between the EIA's own two endpoint coordinates (corrected for the document's own transposed long./lat. column labels, as previously identified in this batch's route-creation pass) is 30.9 km -- consistent with a 33 km pipe route (7% routing overhead, plausible for a route the EIA itself describes as running largely straight, parallel to a canal and a road) but incompatible with a 55 km route (78% overhead, implausible for that alignment). (2) INTERNAL CONSISTENCY -- the EIA states the TOTAL duplication project length as 'Abr Sinai 36 inch, 111 KM' in three separate places (the project-purpose paragraph, the sand-volume calculation, and Table 3.2's construction schedule line 'Duplication of Abr Sinai P/L 36 inch 111KM'), which is exactly Loop 1 (33 km) + Loop 2 (78 km, this row's sibling P8044). The sheet's two figures for the same two rows sum to 55+75=130 km, NOT 111 km -- directly contradicting a fact the EIA repeats three times about its own project. (3) MAP CROSS-CHECK -- the sheet's own currently-cited source (EGAS Annual Report 2018, page 35 GASCO national grid map, read visually per this scope's map-reading rule) DOES show a '36 inch - 55 km' label on the correct corridor east of El-Tina, immediately followed eastward by a '36 inch - 75 km' label (matching P8044's sheet value of 75.0 km almost exactly) and then a '36 inch - 196 km' label further east (a different, out-of-scope line) -- so the map's SEGMENT ORDER matches GEM's two-row split exactly, but its LENGTH FIGURES (55/75) disagree with the EIA's own chainage (33/78) for the same two endpoints. This is a genuine disagreement between two non-GEM sources describing the same two segments, not one bad source and one good one -- flagging for human adjudication rather than silently overwriting, but the geodesic and internal-consistency checks both favor the EIA's 33 km as the more likely correct figure for this specific row.
